channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Export Agency Supports Shymkent's Manufacturing Sector Expansion
item.description: Kazakh enterprises in the manufacturing industry are expanding into foreign markets. The Export-Credit Agency of Kazakhstan (ECA) is assisting businesses, like the Shymkent industrial hub, by addressing challenges such as working capital shortages and non-payment risks from foreign clients. ECA's support has reached 28.5 billion tenge for 'Shymkentmay'.

item.title: Four Men Detained in Isfara in Connection with Minor's Case
item.description: Four residents of Isfara's Khonobod jamoat have been detained on suspicion of sexual acts against a minor. According to the Ministry of Internal Affairs for Sughd region, the suspects allegedly engaged in intimate relations with the girl between May and August. Criminal charges have been filed under Tajikistan's Criminal Code.

item.title: Nazarbayev University Rises 100 Places in Prestigious International Ranking for Second Consecutive Year
item.description: Nazarbayev University (NU) has climbed 100 places in a prestigious international ranking for the second year running, now positioned between 376-400 globally. The university maintained its top spot in Kazakhstan and Central Asia. NU's research quality was particularly noted, placing it on par with institutions like the University of Geneva.

item.title: Luxury Cars Imported to Russia via Kyrgyzstan, Baza Reports
item.description: Russian Telegram channel Baza reports that luxury cars, including a Bugatti W16 Mistral worth approximately 5 million euros, are being imported into Russia from Kyrgyzstan. The commercial recycling fee for one vehicle reportedly amounted to 244 million rubles. Kyrgyz authorities have not yet commented on the information.

item.title: NYT: A7 Company Helps Russia Evade Sanctions Through Kyrgyzstan
item.description: The New York Times reports that Russian company A7 used shell companies and cryptocurrency for money laundering and falsified trade documents to circumvent sanctions via Kyrgyzstan. The company allegedly conducted financial operations exceeding $500 million in the first four months of 2025. A7 companies reportedly opened six bank accounts in Kyrgyzstan, handling up to $100 million.

item.title: Kyrgyz Stock Exchange to Develop Islamic Finance Platform with International Association
item.description: The Kyrgyz Stock Exchange (KSE) and the International Association of Partnership Economy and Finance (IAPEF) have signed an agreement to develop an Islamic finance platform. The initiative aims to introduce Islamic finance instruments, including sukuk securities, and train specialists. KSE hopes this will integrate Bishkek into the regional stock market.

item.title: Kazakh President's Official Visit to Germany Continues in Munich
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's official visit to Germany continues in Munich. The head of state will hold meetings with the heads of the Bavarian government and Landtag, as well as business representatives. He will also attend the opening ceremony of the Kazakhstan-Bavaria Technology Forum.

item.title: Uzbekistan's housing market sees accelerating price growth and increased mortgage lending
item.description: Uzbekistan's Central Bank reported that demand and supply in the real estate market grew in Q2 2026, supported by rising incomes and mortgage loans. While overall transactions increased slightly year-on-year, a significant surge in Q1 was attributed to the escrow system's introduction. Khorezm region saw the largest transaction growth.

item.title: Almaty Introduces New Parking Tariffs Ranging from 100 to 200 Tenge Per Hour
item.description: Starting October 4, Almaty will implement new hourly parking rates from 100 to 200 tenge, depending on demand. Low-demand areas will remain at 100 tenge, medium-demand at 150 tenge, and high-demand at 200 tenge. Residents can still obtain permits for one free parking spot.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Small Neighborhood Stores Lose Up to 40% Due to Taxes and Fees
item.description: Kazakh lawmakers propose reducing tax burdens and providing preferential financing for small neighborhood stores, estimating they lose up to 40% of operating profit to taxes and mandatory payments. These stores are crucial in rural areas and small towns where large chains are scarce.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and United Kingdom Discuss Expanding Military Cooperation
item.description: Kyrgyzstan and the United Kingdom are exploring ways to expand cooperation in the military sphere. A meeting between defense representatives focused on the current state of bilateral ties and future development, including experience exchange and joint activities. English language courses for the Kyrgyz Armed Forces were also discussed.

item.title: Kazakhstan Banks No Longer Offer 20% Deposit Yields Amidst Rate Cuts
item.description: Deposit interest rates in Kazakhstan have decreased, with no banks now offering 20% yields. This follows the National Bank's third consecutive reduction of its base rate to 16.25% in September. The highest available rate is now 19.6% on savings deposits with replenishment options.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Largest Banks to Undergo Cybersecurity Attack Readiness Checks
item.description: The major banks in Kazakhstan will be tested for their preparedness against cyberattacks. This measure aims to assess and enhance the security infrastructure of the country's leading financial institutions in the face of evolving digital threats.

item.title: Uzbekistan Sets Cybersecurity Goals for 2026-2030, Enhancing Digital Sovereignty
item.description: Uzbekistan aims to strengthen cybersecurity by 2030, focusing on protecting digital infrastructure and achieving information technology sovereignty. Key initiatives include holding officials accountable, implementing cyber hygiene in schools, and establishing national SOC centers.

item.title: UN Highlights Significant Climate Impact of Food Waste
item.description: Approximately 60% of global food waste originates from households, contributing to 8-10% of worldwide greenhouse gas emissions, according to the UN Environment Programme. This waste, particularly methane from landfills, exacerbates global warming. Reducing food waste is presented as an accessible and cost-effective climate change mitigation strategy.

item.title: Kazakhstan Considers Moratorium on Small and Medium Business Inspections
item.description: Kazakhstan is considering a one-to-two-year moratorium on inspections for small and medium-sized businesses (SMEs) to foster a more favorable operating environment. The proposal, excluding checks related to public safety and emergencies, aims to reduce administrative pressure and shift oversight to a risk-based, digital, and preventive format.

item.title: Kyrgyz Foreign Minister to Visit Ghana for Official Talks
item.description: Jeenbek Kulubaev, the Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Kyrgyz Republic, will undertake an official visit to Ghana from September 30 to October 1. The visit is at the invitation of Ghana's Minister of Foreign Affairs and Regional Integration, Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa.

item.title: Kazakh Interior Ministry denies reports of police contacting post authors after Caspian tragedy
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Internal Affairs has denied reports that police contacted social media users to delete posts following a tragedy on the Caspian Sea. First Deputy Minister Sanjar Adilov stated that police did not make any such calls. Officers worked in an enhanced mode to ensure public order after 14 servicemen died during a naval exercise due to severe weather.

item.title: Three individuals arrested in Kazakhstan for distributing personal data
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Internal Affairs is investigating three criminal cases related to the distribution of personal data, with three individuals arrested and remanded in custody by court order. The investigation is ongoing. The ministry is also considering strengthening liability for personal data leaks, including increasing fines for large companies.

item.title: US troops fully withdraw from Iraq, raising concerns about increased Iranian influence
item.description: US troops are fully withdrawing from Iraq, a move that experts believe could strengthen Iran's influence and that of its allies in the country. Security expert Jasim al-Bahadli suggests the withdrawal weakens a military force that countered Iranian influence. Pro-Iranian armed groups have called the withdrawal a 'historic victory'.

item.title: Unaccounted goods discovered during tax inspection in Kyrgyzstan's Kara-Suu district
item.description: State Tax Service employees in Kyrgyzstan's Kara-Suu district of Osh region detected a violation of tax legislation during a raid. The violation involved the import of unaccounted goods into the Kyrgyz Republic.

item.title: Flydubai Pilot Allegedly Attempted to Crash Plane with Passengers Aboard
item.description: An investigation is underway in Israel into claims that a Flydubai pilot attempted to intentionally crash a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv. Passengers and crew reportedly intervened to subdue the pilot after a struggle in the cockpit. The aircraft made a safe emergency landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, with all passengers unharmed.

item.title: Woman Who Reported Suspected Abuse Found Dead Day After Police Released Husband
item.description: A woman who reported her husband for suspected abuse was found dead the day after police released him. The husband claims they argued, and she attacked him first. Police had detained him but released him hours later. The woman's relatives allege the investigation is biased.

item.title: State Award Established for Educators Named After Abdulla Avloniy
item.description: Uzbekistan will establish a state award named after Abdulla Avloniy to recognize outstanding educators across all levels of education. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev proposed the award to encourage and incentivize advanced pedagogical practices.

item.title: Kazakhstan MP Proposes Support for Families Not Receiving Alimony
item.description: A Member of Parliament in Kazakhstan has proposed targeted support measures for families who do not receive alimony payments. The proposal also calls for increased control over debtors' actual incomes and the effectiveness of enforcement. Many mothers reportedly raise children alone, facing significant financial burdens, especially for children with disabilities.

item.title: Kazakhstan MP Proposes Comprehensive Approach to Alimony Enforcement
item.description: A Member of Parliament in Kazakhstan has proposed a comprehensive system for enforcing alimony obligations, moving beyond just increasing penalties for debtors. The deputy highlighted cases where court decisions are not practically helping children, especially those with disabilities, due to debtors hiding income. The current system's effectiveness is questioned.

item.title: UNDP supports families in Kunduz with irrigation, land clearing, and business aid
item.description: The UNDP is helping families in Kunduz, Afghanistan, strengthen livelihoods by improving irrigation, clearing landmines, and supporting local businesses. These efforts aim to create economic opportunities and help communities cope with an increase in returnees. The program is implemented with international partners and funding from Japan and the UN Special Trust Fund.

item.title: Kazakhstan re-evaluates ethnic Kazakh returnees, treating them as migrant workers
item.description: Kazakhstan has reportedly begun assessing ethnic Kazakh returnees ('kandas') similarly to ordinary migrant workers, potentially impacting their status and benefits. The article questions the reasons behind this shift in policy.

item.title: Foreign nationals arrested for organizing prostitution ring in Dushanbe hotel
item.description: Dushanbe police have uncovered a prostitution ring organized by foreign nationals in the Hulbuk Palace hotel. Several women, also foreign citizens, were allegedly involved in providing sexual services for money. Criminal charges have been filed, and those involved face deportation.

item.title: Kazakhstan Seeks New Oil and Gas Resources as Reserves Deplete
item.description: Kazakhstan's existing oil and gas fields are nearly 70% depleted, prompting a search for new resources. KazMunayGas is developing projects with billions of tons of potential fuel equivalent. The company plans to form a consortium with major international oil and gas firms. A new strategy focuses on 32 promising fields out of 143, aiming to increase oil recovery rates.

item.title: Kazakh MP Proposes Unified Digital Security System for Military Training
item.description: Kazakh Member of Parliament Abbat Orisbayev has submitted a deputy's inquiry to Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov, proposing the implementation of a unified digital security system for military and special training exercises. He emphasized that the safety and security of military personnel and rescuers must be paramount. The proposal includes continuous drone monitoring, electronic identification tags, and automatic alarm systems for emergencies.

item.title: Central Asia's Evolving Importance Beyond Minerals and Geopolitics
item.description: Central Asia's growing significance stems from its internal transformation, not just minerals or competition with China. Over three decades, the region has worked to improve governance and transparency, making it more attractive to investors. Uzbekistan exemplifies this with economic liberalization reforms since 2017.

item.title: Uzbekistan: Nearly $46 Million Earned from Solar Energy Sales to State
item.description: From January to August, residents of Uzbekistan earned nearly $46 million by selling surplus solar energy to the state grid. Over 61,500 citizens participated in the 'Sunny Home' program in August, generating 105.4 million kWh. Bukhara region received the most subsidies.

item.title: Kazakh Interior Ministry comments on attacks targeting Kazakh citizens' accounts
item.description: Kazakhstan's Deputy Interior Minister Sanzhar Adil told a briefing that cases of account blocking and attacks on WhatsApp, including those targeting journalists, were investigated. He clarified that these were not cybercrimes but social engineering tactics, with related issues falling under the Ministry of Culture and Information's purview. A pre-trial investigation has been initiated regarding reports of over 200 messages from unknown numbers and bot attacks.

item.title: Russia Restricts Cash Ruble Exports to Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, and EAEU Countries
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin has signed a decree limiting the export of cash rubles from Russia to Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, Azerbaijan, and EAEU member states. Individuals can export up to 1 million rubles, while legal entities and individual entrepreneurs are prohibited from exporting cash rubles regardless of the amount. Exceptions apply for specific airports and diplomatic missions.

item.title: Kazakhstan Interior Ministry comments on journalist account blocks: 'These were not hacks'
item.description: Kazakhstan's Vice Minister of Internal Affairs Sanzhar Adil told a briefing that blocks on journalists' accounts were not hacks but likely social engineering. The ministry conducted an investigation into the access issues reported by independent journalists.

item.title: Tajikistan to Increase Electricity Exports to Afghanistan
item.description: Tajikistan's electricity company has agreed to increase electricity exports to Afghanistan, according to the Taliban-controlled Afghanistan Electricity Company (DABS). Discussions included expanding transmission lines, improving quality, and tariffs. A plan for a 500-kilovolt transmission line was presented.

item.title: Afghanistan and Tajikistan Discuss Increased Electricity Imports and New Transmission Line
item.description: Afghanistan and Tajikistan held discussions on increasing electricity imports and expanding energy sector cooperation, including plans for a new 500-kilovolt transmission line. Technical and commercial teams will continue negotiations to achieve practical outcomes on the discussed issues.

item.title: Suspect Arrested for Assaulting Student at Religious School in Takhar
item.description: Taliban security forces in Takhar have arrested a suspect identified as Qari Karam, aged 21, for assaulting a student at a religious school in the Rostaq district. The arrest follows a viral video showing the assault, prompting public calls for an end to violence in educational centers.

item.title: Flydubai Flight to Israel Diverted to Saudi Arabia After Hijacking Alert
item.description: An Israeli media report indicates a Flydubai flight bound for Tel Aviv was diverted to Saudi Arabia after issuing emergency signals, including a hijacking code. The aircraft reportedly transmitted code 7700 for general emergency, followed briefly by code 7500, signifying unlawful interference. Israeli fighter jets were scrambled, and an emergency security meeting was held. Sources later suggested the alerts stemmed from a dispute between pilots.
